battlefield.note: The strait between the island of Salamis and the coast of Attica, the islet of Psyttaleia at its mouth, a narrow channel round the north of the island and Mount Aigaleos above the shore.

popup.title: Salamis: The Narrow Strait
popup.body:
You command the allied Greek fleet in the strait between Salamis and Attica. The Persians have more ships, coming in line after line, but in the narrows they cannot spread out or turn: keep your triremes together, beat each squadron before the next arrives, and keep clear of the Attic shore, where Persian archers are watching. Your crews know these waters. Ship counters stand for squadrons.

Objective: Sink the Persian fleet.

In September 480 BCE Themistocles lured the Persian fleet into the strait of Salamis, where the Greek triremes, fewer but better handled in the narrow water, broke it while Xerxes watched from the shore. The defeat ended the Persian invasion by sea.

popup.title: The Persians row into the strait
popup.body: At dawn the Persian fleet comes into the narrows in long columns. Here their numbers cannot spread out: meet the leading squadrons together and ram them as their lines bunch up.

popup.title: The Egyptian squadron
popup.body: Ships sent round Salamis in the night are coming down the western channel behind you. Turn part of your line to meet them.

popup.title: The second line
popup.body: More Persian squadrons are pushing in behind the first and fouling one another in the narrows.

popup.title: The Aeginetan ambush
popup.body: The Aeginetan squadron has been waiting at the mouth of the strait. Persian ships that turn back for the open gulf will run into it.

popup.title: Xerxes watches
popup.body: From his throne on Mount Aigaleos the king is watching his fleet break up. Sink what is left of it.
